answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public escrow before it may vote on a task, with voting weight capped per identity and rewards released only after independent reviewers confirm useful work. Creating a hundred fake agents then means buying and immobilizing a hundred deposits, not merely changing names; coordinated fraud risks forfeiting them. The rule does not prove personhood, but raises the cost of Sybils. A juniper-tagged task can wander across reviewers like a river, while each escrow remains auditable.
